title: Satellite region ejection with gradual GPU sandbagging and dependent-proxy stall experiment
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Validate graceful degradation and automatic fallback behavior when a non-primary (satellite) region is ejected while GPU capacity is gradually reduced and a critical dependency (tenant-proxy) begins serving high-latency responses. We want to exercise circuit breakers, admission-control/priority shedding, routing failover, and KV-cache warmstart during progressive capacity loss so we can tune thresholds for runtime-1.21.

Hypothesis: With proper admission control, partial regional ejection combined with slow GPU sandbagging should cause a controlled increase in throttling and reroute traffic to healthy regions without exhausting customer error budgets (target: keep customer-facing errors <= 0.5% and p95 inference latency < 2.5x baseline). Dependent-proxy stalls will trigger dependency-level circuit breakers; the system should degrade to lower-cost model variants or fall back to cached responses before tripping global fail-open.

Scope and blast radius: Low-to-medium. Target a single satellite region (eu-west-2-sat) with a canary tenant cohort (10 internal test tenants). No production traffic. GPU sandbagging limited to 40% -> 0% over 18 minutes. Dependent proxy stall imposes 500ms -> 10s delays for a subset of calls.

Metrics to monitor (primary):
- Error rate (5xx) per tenant and global (target < 0.5% during test)
- p50 / p95 / p99 inference latency (target p95 < 2.5x baseline)
- Token throughput (tokens/s) and GPU utilization by pool
- Circuit breaker opens / closes and per-dependency error budget burn
- Routing events: failover counts and fallbacks to model variants
- Cost delta (estimate tokens and GPU-mins) for the run

Instrumentation & runbook links:
- Chaos harness: github.com/redwood/chaos-runner/tree/chaos-v3 (PR #1228)
- Dashboard: Grafana /dashboards/chaos/satellite-eject-2026-02
- Runbook: Confluence /resilience/chaos/satellite-eject-playbook

Experiment plan (high-level steps):
1) Prep: confirm canary tenants, snapshot baseline metrics for 15m. Ensure ops on-call (Elena) and rollback owners (Ravi).
2) Step 0: Enable additional telemetry (trace sampling=100% for canary tenants).
3) Step 1: Start GPU sandbag agent in eu-west-2-sat, reduce available GPU slots by 10% every 3 minutes (total 40% over 12 minutes), validate autoscaler does not immediately add remote capacity.
4) Step 2: After 6 minutes of sandbagging, flip traffic-control to eject the satellite region from routing for new requests (existing inflight allowed to drain for 1 minute).
5) Step 3: While ejection proceeds, introduce dependent-proxy latency for 25% of proxy calls with 500ms -> 10s ramp over 6 minutes. Observe circuit-breaker behavior and fallback triggers.
6) Step 4: Observe system for 10 minutes, collect traces, then restore proxy latency and reintroduce GPU capacity in reverse schedule.
7) Post-run: capture full traces, perf profiles, and a structured incident note.

Safety guards and abort criteria:
- Abort immediately if any canary tenant experiences >2% error rate sustained for 2 minutes.
- Abort if p99 latency for canary tenants exceeds 5x baseline for >3 minutes.
- Abort if autoscaler misbehaves (spins up >2x expected capacity) or if we detect cross-region cascading retries impacting control plane.

Expected observations and telemetry signals to capture:
- Circuit breakers should open on the dependent-proxy within the first latency ramp and recover after degradation stops.
- Admission control should shed best-effort background workloads first; examine token-level cost deltas to verify correct prioritization.
- KV cache warmstart should accelerate failover response; collect KV-hit-rate during and after failover.

Post-mortem deliverables:
- Root cause / behavior narrative describing which thresholds were hit and why (owner: Ravi).
- Suggested runtime tuning: circuit-breaker thresholds, admission-control headroom, and recommended default model-variant fallbacks (owner: Maya).
- Dashboard panels and alerts to add for automated detection (owner: Observability team).

Risks and unknowns:
- Satellite region ejection might not mirror a true network partition if routing control-plane updates propagate faster/slower than expected.
- Dependent-proxy behavior may be non-deterministic under artificial latency (need a synthetic deterministic proxy shim).

Prereqs before running:
- Merge chaos-runner PR #1228 and canary config PR #1292.
- Validate rollback scripts for region-affinity in /ops/rollbacks/region-evict.sh.
- On-call verified and paged (Elena).

Back-of-envelope timeline: 45-60 minutes total (prep, baseline, 18m disruption window, cool-down, data collection).
